correctness.rationale: The primary reduction fixes the proposition vocabulary, one-agent initial state, and goal independently of the PCP instance. All PCP dependence lies in the finite add_i event models, plus three fixed verifier actions. Theorem 3.19 gives the exact match-plan equivalence. The restricted planning problem is r.e. because finite plans can be enumerated and finite product updates checked effectively. Binary PCP is r.e.-complete, using a computable prefix-code reduction from arbitrary finite alphabets if needed.

originality.rationale: The 2026 source states undecidability but not fixed-state/fixed-goal input localization or r.e.-completeness. The 2018 small-epistemic-planning result fixes actions and goal while varying the initial state, so it does not imply the accepted action-only-input theorem.
residual_risks: The fixed-state observation is immediate after a close read of the source construction and may be viewed as an unstated corollary rather than a distant theorem.

Earlier epistemic-planning papers may contain a fixed-initial-state reduction under different action semantics, but none located combines the exact one-agent K, depth-one-precondition, no-postcondition restrictions.
The action library remains unbounded, so the theorem does not subsume fixed-action undecidability results.

The accepted theorem localizes all instance information to the action library in the newly resolved modal-depth-one/no-postcondition setting, complementing the known fixed-action/varying-state construction.
